title: Model Variant Lifter: Guided version selection & performance dossier
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a guided console flow and read-only dossier for choosing and pinning model versions across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. The feature should help engineers and product owners compare performance profiles (latency, throughput, quality regressions) and choose a safe pin strategy (exact vs. fuzzy vs. semantic pin), plus publish the chosen performance profile for downstream observability and rollout policies.
acceptance_criteria: Console surfaces a ‘Compare versions’ panel showing side-by-side performance metrics (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, eval pass rate) for up to 4 versions
Users can select a target version and choose a pin scope: exact build, major+minor, or semantic alias, with an explanation of trade-offs
Publish action creates a version pin event that appears in audit logs and triggers perf-profile publication to the Optimize service
A published profile includes the test set used, date, dataset link, quantization/compile flags, and observed SLO deltas
Canary rollout wiring: selecting ‘Enable canary’ shows options for traffic percentage, duration, and automatic rollback thresholds
All actions have inline contextual help and links to full evaluation artifacts (Figma/Confluence/Drive), and the UX meets accessibility contrast and keyboard-nav checks
tasks: Design: create comparison panel mocks and tooltip language for pin scopes (DES-9012)
API: extend model-metadata endpoint to return published perf-profile artifacts (ENG-6843)
Backend: implement pin event store and audit entry (ENG-6891)
Console: build new compare UI, publish button, and canary experience (ENG-7210)
E2E: add smoke tests for publish+canary flows and audit entries
Docs: update onboarding guide and changelog with new pin semantics
engineering_notes: Perf metric normalization: backend will return latency histograms and cost per 1k tokens; console should compute percent deltas and highlight regressions >5%
Publish payload needs fields: version, build_hash, compile_flags, quantization_profile, eval_suite_id, dataset_sha, measured_metrics_snapshot_url
Audit entries must include actor, timestamp, prior_pin_state, new_pin_state, and optional release notes
Canary controller will be implemented as a policy in Dedicated routing layer; console only sends configuration and receives status updates
qa_plan: QA to validate metric accuracy (compare console numbers to tracing dashboard), verify audit log entries for publish/pin actions, simulate canary with feature-flagged controller and confirm rollback triggers on synthetic error injection.
rollout_plan: Start with internal beta in Redwood staging + 3 customers on Dedicated. Monitor Console telemetry (clicks, publish failures) and Optimize ingestion metrics for published profiles. Gradual ramp over 3 weeks with weekly checkpoints.
